method: Restarted backend through Crucible settings, created a fresh chat at user request, ran the same 700-line/two-file batch prompt and a citation-rule follow-up. Eight-action bound per turn; both answered normally at or below the bound and were verified in VS Code. No edits requested or executed.

read.goal: Read lines 1-700 of services/agentd-py/agentd/chat/controller_prompts.py and all of services/agentd-py/agentd/chat/batch_history.py. These reads are independent; issue both read_file calls in one tool_calls batch. The 700-line range is intentional to test adaptive read delivery beyond the old 500-line ceiling. Then briefly explain where the tool_calls action description is defined and what interrupted_history does. Do not modify files.
read.answer:
The `tool_calls` action description is defined in `services/agentd-py/agentd/chat/controller_prompts.py` within `_VARIANT_SPECS["tool_calls"]` at lines 241–250. Its description says to use workspace tools only when needed, choose tools from the available catalog, and provide schema-matching arguments; it requires a non-empty `calls` array (lines 242–249). The surrounding prompt also documents batch scheduling and independent parallel calls at lines 252–275.

`interrupted_history` in `services/agentd-py/agentd/chat/batch_history.py` (lines 6–19) returns a copied history list. For entries belonging to a batch, with role `tool_result`, and status `pending`, `waiting_approval`, or `running`, it changes the status to `interrupted`, marks `is_error=True`, and replaces the content with a message stating that the prior execution was interrupted and was not replayed. All other entries are copied unchanged, preserving completed results and preventing side effects from being replayed.

followup.goal: Can you point me to the controller prompt text that governs reusing code already read in this chat, and explain when reading it again is necessary? Do not modify files.
followup.answer:
The governing text is in `services/agentd-py/agentd/chat/controller_prompts.py:375-383`.

It says to locate the exact file and line before reading, avoid blindly calling `read_file`, and not re-issue an identical read whose result is already available. It also says to reuse visible evidence from successful tool results, including earlier turns.

Read the code again only when:
- the earlier result was missing or truncated;
- a freshness check is needed because the file may have changed.

For code-specific answers, the prompt still requires that the actual function or code you cite has been read; outlines and bare file names are insufficient. Once the concrete files/functions are read and further reads would not change the answer, exploration should stop (`controller_prompts.py:378-389`).

result: New citation and continuation instructions reach native requests, but redundant tool use persists. Actual truncation recovery is correct; the initial test adds a graph query, failed fixed-string search, and overlapping read after full delivery. Follow-up performs one unnecessary unchanged reread then answers. This does not establish a causal improvement.
read_budget_note: Delivered chunks were 1-128,129-379,380-570,571-700. Earlier chunks report character truncation. About 16k characters for single reads matches the conservative unknown-capacity fallback in read_policy.py; capacity state itself was not captured. A fresh-thread comparison therefore differs from the earlier full-700-line delivery.
remaining_candidate: query_graph catalog says to use it after read_file; its no-node result directs search_code then retry. In this trace the graph detour produced that correction, a wrongly escaped fixed-string search, and a redundant read. This is a plausible contributor, not proven sole cause.
